revisions.title: From a private prompt to Socrates’ declaration
revisions.body: Menexenus, the returning boy, is beside Lysis when Lysis quietly asks Socrates to tell him what he has been saying to Lysis. Socrates accepts the turn and directs the exchange toward questioning Menexenus. He then frames that move through self-characterization: he is intensely devoted to acquiring friends, valuing a good friend above horses, dogs, gold, honors, and even Darius himself.
